Post-Contingency Power Transfer Distribution Factor (PTDF) Update

PTDF Matrix

As discussed earlier, the nominal PTDF matrix \(H^0\in\mathbb R^{L\times N}\) can be written as follows:

\[ \begin{array}{rrccccccc} & & & \text{Bus 1} & \text{Bus 2} & \cdots & \text{Bus }n & \text{Ref Bus} & \\ H^0= & \begin{array}{r}\text{Branch 1}\vphantom{H^0_{\ell n}}\\\text{Branch 2}\vphantom{H^0_{\ell n}}\\\vdots\vphantom{\vdots}\\\text{Branch }\ell\vphantom{H^0_{\ell n}}\end{array} & \left[\vphantom{\begin{array}{c}H^0_{11}\vphantom{H^0_{\ell n}}\\H^0_{21}\vphantom{H^0_{\ell n}}\\\vdots\vphantom{\vdots}\\H^0_{\ell1}\vphantom{H^0_{\ell n}}\end{array}}\right. & \begin{array}{c}H^0_{11}\vphantom{H^0_{\ell n}}\\H^0_{21}\vphantom{H^0_{\ell n}}\\\vdots\vphantom{\vdots}\\H^0_{\ell1}\vphantom{H^0_{\ell n}}\end{array} & \begin{array}{c}H^0_{12}\vphantom{H^0_{\ell n}}\\H^0_{22}\vphantom{H^0_{\ell n}}\\\vdots\vphantom{\vdots}\\H^0_{\ell2}\vphantom{H^0_{\ell n}}\end{array} & \begin{array}{c}\cdots\vphantom{H^0_{\ell n}}\\\cdots\vphantom{H^0_{\ell n}}\\\ddots\vphantom{\vdots}\\\cdots\vphantom{H^0_{\ell n}}\end{array} & \begin{array}{c}H^0_{1n}\vphantom{H^0_{\ell n}}\\H^0_{2n}\vphantom{H^0_{\ell n}}\\\vdots\vphantom{\vdots}\\H^0_{\ell n}\vphantom{H^0_{\ell n}}\end{array} & \begin{array}{c}0\vphantom{H^0_{\ell n}}\\0\vphantom{H^0_{\ell n}}\\\vdots\vphantom{\vdots}\\0\vphantom{H^0_{\ell n}}\end{array} & \left.\vphantom{\begin{array}{c}H^0_{11}\vphantom{H^0_{\ell n}}\\H^0_{21}\vphantom{H^0_{\ell n}}\\\vdots\vphantom{\vdots}\\H^0_{\ell1}\vphantom{H^0_{\ell n}}\end{array}}\right] \end{array}. \]

\(H^0_{\ell n}\): If we inject 1 MW at bus \(n\) and withdraw 1 MW at the reference bus, how much would the power flow change on the monitored branch \(\ell\)? [1]

Question: Why is the last column of \(H^0\) zero?
Answer: The last column corresponds to the reference bus. For this column, the 1 MW injection and 1 MW withdrawal occur at the same bus and cancel out. No branch flow changes, so every entry in the column is zero.

Preparations

Suppose we have \(N\) buses and \(m\) outage lines:

\[ O=(o_1,\ldots,o_m). \]

For each outage line \(o_j\), define \(d_{o_j}\in\mathbb R^{N\times1}\) to represent its source-sink pair:

\[ d_{o_j}=\begin{bmatrix} 0\\0\\\vdots\\1\\\vdots\\-1\\\vdots\\0 \end{bmatrix}. \]

Source bus \(s_j\): \(+1\). Sink bus \(t_j\): \(-1\).

For \(m\) outage lines, define the incidence matrix \(D\in\mathbb R^{N\times m}\):

\[ D=\begin{bmatrix}d_{o_1}&d_{o_2}&\cdots&d_{o_m}\end{bmatrix} =\left[ \underbrace{\begin{bmatrix}0\\\vdots\\1\\\vdots\\-1\\\vdots\\0\end{bmatrix}}_{d_{o_1}} \quad\underbrace{\begin{bmatrix}0\\1\\\vdots\\0\\\vdots\\-1\\0\end{bmatrix}}_{d_{o_2}} \quad\cdots\quad \underbrace{\begin{bmatrix}-1\\\vdots\\0\\\vdots\\0\\\vdots\\1\end{bmatrix}}_{d_{o_m}} \right]. \]

Branch-flow sensitivities to outage-branch endpoint injections form the matrix \(T\in\mathbb R^{L\times m}\). Its element \(T_{\ell j}\) gives the change in flow on branch \(\ell\) per 1 MW injected at the from bus and withdrawn at the to bus of branch \(o_j\) scheduled for outage, while all branches are still in service. Each element of \(T\) is a shift-factor difference (shift spread).

\[ T=H^0D= \begin{bmatrix} H^0_{1,s_1}-H^0_{1,t_1} & \cdots & H^0_{1,s_m}-H^0_{1,t_m}\\ H^0_{2,s_1}-H^0_{2,t_1} & \cdots & H^0_{2,s_m}-H^0_{2,t_m}\\ \vdots & \ddots & \vdots\\ H^0_{\ell,s_1}-H^0_{\ell,t_1} & \cdots & H^0_{\ell,s_m}-H^0_{\ell,t_m} \end{bmatrix}. \]

\[ T_O= \begin{bmatrix} H^0_{o_1,s_1}-H^0_{o_1,t_1} & \cdots & H^0_{o_1,s_m}-H^0_{o_1,t_m}\\ H^0_{o_2,s_1}-H^0_{o_2,t_1} & \cdots & H^0_{o_2,s_m}-H^0_{o_2,t_m}\\ \vdots & \ddots & \vdots\\ H^0_{o_m,s_1}-H^0_{o_m,t_1} & \cdots & H^0_{o_m,s_m}-H^0_{o_m,t_m} \end{bmatrix} \in\mathbb R^{m\times m}. \]

Extract the rows of \(T\) corresponding to the outage lines to form \(T_O\). Its off-diagonal entries describe how an endpoint transfer associated with one outage branch affects the flow on another branch scheduled for outage.

Define \(A=I-T_O\), where \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) and \(I\) is the identity matrix:

\[ A=I-T_O= \begin{bmatrix} 1-(H^0_{o_1,s_1}-H^0_{o_1,t_1}) & \cdots & -(H^0_{o_1,s_m}-H^0_{o_1,t_m})\\ \vdots & \ddots & \vdots\\ -(H^0_{o_m,s_1}-H^0_{o_m,t_1}) & \cdots & 1-(H^0_{o_m,s_m}-H^0_{o_m,t_m}) \end{bmatrix}. \]

Define \(q\in\mathbb R^{N\times1}\) as the nodal net injection vector. Each element corresponds to the injection at a bus:

\[ q=\begin{bmatrix}q_1\\q_2\\\vdots\\q_N\end{bmatrix}, \qquad \sum_{i=1}^Nq_i=0. \]

Define \(f=H^0q\in\mathbb R^L\) as the nominal branch-flow vector, containing the flow on each branch:

\[ f=\begin{bmatrix}f_1\\\vdots\\f_L\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} H^0_{1,1}&\cdots&H^0_{1,N}\\ \vdots&\ddots&\vdots\\ H^0_{L,1}&\cdots&H^0_{L,N} \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix}q_1\\\vdots\\q_N\end{bmatrix}. \]

This completes the preparations.

Handling the Contingency

Figure 1. Black dots represent buses, the blue line is the line scheduled for outage, and red dashed lines represent connections to the rest of the grid. (a) Stage 1: Nominal. (b) Stage 2: Add a virtual transfer. (c) Stage 3: Remove the line and the virtual transfer together.

Stage 1: Nominal

\[ q_{\mathrm{in}}=q_{\mathrm{out}}+f. \tag{1} \]

Stage 2: Add a virtual transfer

\[ c+q_{\mathrm{in}}^{\prime}=q_{\mathrm{out}}^{\prime}+\widetilde f. \tag{2} \]

Stage 3: If \(c=\widetilde f\), remove the line and the virtual transfer together

\[ q_{\mathrm{in}}^{\prime}=q_{\mathrm{out}}^{\prime}. \tag{3} \]

The idea here is to add a virtual transfer from the source node to the sink node, which changes the power flows in the grid. After that, we remove the target line and the virtual transfer together. If the virtual transfer is exactly equal to the power flow on the outage line after the transfer is added, then power balance still holds. Therefore, the flows on the remaining lines are the post-outage flows.

Let’s explore the math.

For each scheduled outage line \(o_j\), let’s add a virtual transfer \(c_{o_j}\) MW. The transfer vector is \(c_O\in\mathbb R^m\):

\[ c_O=\begin{bmatrix}c_{o_1}\\c_{o_2}\\\vdots\\c_{o_m}\end{bmatrix}. \]

The flows with the virtual transfers added are

\[ \widetilde f=f+Tc_O. \]

\[ \begin{bmatrix}\widetilde f_1\\\vdots\\\widetilde f_L\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}f_1\\\vdots\\f_L\end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} T_{1,1}&\cdots&T_{1,m}\\ \vdots&\ddots&\vdots\\ T_{L,1}&\cdots&T_{L,m} \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix}c_{o_1}\\\vdots\\c_{o_m}\end{bmatrix}. \]

Remove the virtual transfer and the scheduled outage line together!

Combining (2) and (3) gives the condition for each outage line:

\[ c_{o_j}=\widetilde f_{o_j}. \]

Consider the outage line set. The virtual transfer vector satisfies

\[ c_O=\widetilde f_O=f_O+T_Oc_O. \]

Therefore, the virtual transfers satisfy

\[ (I-T_O)c_O=f_O \quad\Longrightarrow\quad Ac_O=f_O \quad\Longrightarrow\quad c_O=A^{-1}f_O. \]

Written out,

\[ \begin{bmatrix} c_{o_1}\\c_{o_2}\\\vdots\\c_{o_m} \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1-T_{o_1,1} & -T_{o_1,2} & \cdots & -T_{o_1,m}\\ -T_{o_2,1} & 1-T_{o_2,2} & \cdots & -T_{o_2,m}\\ \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots\\ -T_{o_m,1} & -T_{o_m,2} & \cdots & 1-T_{o_m,m} \end{bmatrix}^{-1} \begin{bmatrix} f_{o_1}\\f_{o_2}\\\vdots\\f_{o_m} \end{bmatrix}. \]

Power Flow Update

The post-outage flow on each line is

\[ f_\ell^O= \begin{cases} 0, & \ell\in O,\\[4pt] f_\ell+\displaystyle\sum_{j=1}^{m}T_{\ell j}c_{o_j}, & \ell\notin O. \end{cases} \]

Updating the PTDF Matrix

Apply the correction to all PTDF columns:

\[ \widehat H=H^0+TA^{-1}H^0_{O,:}. \]

Substitute \(c_O=A^{-1}f_O\) and \(f_O=H^0_{O,:}q\) into the flow update for the remaining lines, indexed by \(\bar O\):

\[ \begin{aligned} f^O_{\bar O} &=f_{\bar O}+T_{\bar O,:}c_O\\ &=H^0_{\bar O,:}q+T_{\bar O,:}A^{-1}H^0_{O,:}q\\ &=\left(H^0_{\bar O,:}+T_{\bar O,:}A^{-1}H^0_{O,:}\right)q. \end{aligned} \]

The matrix multiplying \(q\) is the updated PTDF for the remaining lines. Thus \(T_{\bar O,:}A^{-1}H^0_{O,:}\) is the PTDF correction, and multiplying it by \(q\) gives the flow change on the remaining lines.

Written out,

\[ \begin{aligned} \widehat H &=\begin{bmatrix} H^0_{11}&H^0_{12}&\cdots&H^0_{1n}&0\\ H^0_{21}&H^0_{22}&\cdots&H^0_{2n}&0\\ \vdots&\vdots&\ddots&\vdots&\vdots\\ H^0_{\ell1}&H^0_{\ell2}&\cdots&H^0_{\ell n}&0 \end{bmatrix}\\[6pt] &\quad+ \begin{bmatrix} T_{1,1}&T_{1,2}&\cdots&T_{1,m}\\ T_{2,1}&T_{2,2}&\cdots&T_{2,m}\\ \vdots&\vdots&\ddots&\vdots\\ T_{\ell,1}&T_{\ell,2}&\cdots&T_{\ell,m} \end{bmatrix} A^{-1} \begin{bmatrix} H^0_{o_1,1}&H^0_{o_1,2}&\cdots&H^0_{o_1,n}&0\\ H^0_{o_2,1}&H^0_{o_2,2}&\cdots&H^0_{o_2,n}&0\\ \vdots&\vdots&\ddots&\vdots&\vdots\\ H^0_{o_m,1}&H^0_{o_m,2}&\cdots&H^0_{o_m,n}&0 \end{bmatrix}. \end{aligned} \]

Then set the outage rows to zero to obtain the updated PTDF:

\[ H^O_{\ell n}= \begin{cases} 0, & \ell\in O,\\[4pt] \widehat H_{\ell n}, & \ell\notin O. \end{cases} \]
